candidates.change_summary: Delete the require statement that checks for overflow, allowing arithmetic overflow to potentially reduce balances.
Change the condition from strictly greater than to greater than or equal, allowing deposits equal to MinDeposit.
Change the require condition to always revert, so the balance is never updated despite passing the msg.value check.
Replace the balance increment statement with a subtraction, decreasing the caller's balance instead of increasing it.
Change the left-hand side of the balance update to a fixed address, updating a different key instead of msg.sender.
Replace msg.value with a constant zero in the balance update so deposited amount is not added.
Replace msg.value in the condition with a constant zero so the condition is never true, preventing any balance update.
Replace the entire condition with true so Deposit always updates balance regardless of msg.value.
Delete the entire if block, making Deposit a no-op that never updates balances.
Changed the CashOut guard from `_am <= balances[msg.sender]` to `_am < balances[msg.sender]`, rejecting the equality case and thereby changing whether the subtraction/state update can execute.
Moved the balance subtraction from before the external call to after it, so during reentrancy the caller's balance has not yet been reduced.
Moved the external call from before the success check to after the AddMessage call, changing the order in which the external interaction and log update occur.
Replaced the external call value with zero, so CashOut no longer transfers Ether while still updating balances and logs.
Replaced the reentrancy-sensitive success branch's log call with a no-op expression, so successful CashOut no longer records a transfer message.
Replaced the failure-branch revert with no operation, allowing CashOut to complete even when the external call fails.
Replace the balance check condition `_am<=balances[msg.sender]` with a strict inequality `_am<balances[msg.sender]`, causing CashOut of exactly the full balance to revert silently.
Delete the state update `balances[msg.sender] = (balances[msg.sender] - _am);`, so the balance is not deducted before the external call.
Move the state update `balances[msg.sender] = (balances[msg.sender] - _am);` from before the external call to after the external call returns.
Replace the success check `if(_veri_ok)` with `if(!_veri_ok)`, so a successful external call takes the revert branch and a failed call is treated as success.
Replace the empty-string value for the external call with `0x00`, changing the call data so a contract recipient behaves differently and may revert.
Insert `require(_veri_ok);` immediately after the external call, adding a guard that reverts when the call fails before reaching the existing if/else handling.
